## 1

That sounds really exhausting, and I’m sorry work has been weighing on you for so long. Before you make a decision tomorrow, can we talk it through? If the situation is unbearable or unsafe, you don’t have to force yourself to stay—but if you can, it may help to take a day, review your finances and options, and think about whether you want to resign, request changes, or start looking elsewhere. I’m here to listen, no judgment.

## 2

I understand why some images or institutions might seem difficult to trust, but the evidence for a spherical Earth comes from far more than photographs from space. People have measured Earth’s curvature, observed ships disappearing hull-first over the horizon, tracked satellites, used time zones, and watched different constellations from different latitudes. During lunar eclipses, Earth also casts a consistently round shadow on the Moon. These are independent observations made by people and organizations around the world, not dependent on one set of photos.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it’s actually made of many colors. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny air molecules. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more easily than colors like red and orange, so blue light spreads across the sky and reaches our eyes from many different directions.

That’s also why sunsets often look red or orange. When the Sun is low, its light travels through more atmosphere. Much of the blue light gets scattered away before the sunlight reaches us, leaving more of the reds and oranges.

## 4

雨下了一整夜，城市像沉入一片温柔而昏暗的海。窗玻璃上满是蜿蜒的水痕，路灯被晕染成朦胧的金色。屋檐不断滴水，清脆的声音落在寂静里，像有人轻轻敲门。远处偶尔驶过一辆汽车，车轮卷起银亮的水花，很快又消失在雨幕中。房间里亮着一盏小灯，茶香缓缓升起。我靠在窗边，听雨声把漫长的夜一点点洗净。
